text: right ok that makes sense. but it also doesnt, like uh, hmm... in the sense of the fact we have a primitive that can take a virtual machine -> render as a texture, and then therefore forever on forward, react doesnt know jack about shit for what is going on, it just knows i have to keep this rendering. so i guess my question is why isnt the hostKey={model.key} effectively treated the same. like here is something you point at, but all you need to know is where to look. and nothing past that
resolution: Answered why hostKey is not treated like the VM-to-texture surface (stable 'here is where to look' pointer). Explanation delivered: the framework runs two identity idioms — stable-location-with-mutable-content (textures/surfaces, dirty-band updates) and content-addressing (ruled house discipline for baked assets, V29/V31, invalidate-by-rename). The edit mesh is the system's one mutable live document but inherited the immutable-asset idiom for topology changes because renaming gave every downstream cache invalidation for free; the price is that every holder of the old name must be chased down, which is the adoption-failure class. Noted the same subsystem already proves the stable idiom works (drag path patches GPU vertices in place at the same offset; paint atlas texture is created once and updated by dirty row bands). Stated what a stable document handle requires: generation tracking inside the GPU intern and paint target (which also fixes the never-evicting retained buffer) and moving topology-changed news onto the existing push ring. No code changed — explanation only; offered to spec the stable-handle design on user go-ahead.
